title: Using AI Code Generation to Migrate 20000 Tests
summary: Slack staff engineer describes migrating 20,000 Enzyme tests to React Testing Library by combining AST codemods with LLMs, and argues for small scopes, context collection and developer review.

assertions.quote: AI by itself was not very successful tool

verdicts.note: Migration case studies (Google, Amazon Java upgrades, Airbnb) got their scale from pairing LLMs with deterministic tooling and validation rather than free-form generation.

assertions.quote: developers role shifted more to reviewing fixing verifying.

verdicts.note: Surveys and studies (e.g. Faros, Google) report increased PR volume and review load with AI adoption.

assertions.quote: the more context you provide for them uh the better they are

verdicts.note: Relevant org context plausibly cuts rework, but the cited 50% token / one-shot result is a single vendor test, not independent evidence.

assertions.quote: you you have generated so much code that you don't know what it does. You don't know how to validate it.

verdicts.note: GitClear and DORA 2025 data show more churn and duplication and lower delivery stability as AI adoption rises; more code means more to maintain.

assertions.quote: longterm it could be problematic because there is a lot of duplication. Some of the abstractions are not created.

verdicts.note: GitClear's 2024-25 analyses found rising duplicated code and falling refactoring with AI adoption.

assertions.quote: if for example your PR has a lot more code then it would take a longer time for other people to review it

verdicts.note: The SmartBear/Cisco review study found defect detection drops beyond ~200-400 LOC per session; AI makes large PRs cheap to produce.

assertions.quote: the best u result that we got from our tools was when when the scope is so minimal uh the smaller the better.

verdicts.note: Small batches with fast feedback are a strong DORA predictor of delivery performance; DORA 2024 linked AI to larger batches and lower stability.

assertions.quote: it enables some people especially those who possess some of the knowledge but they don't know the programming language

verdicts.note: Tools like Lovable, v0, Replit let non-developers produce working prototypes; widely observed.
